observations_X_t: x1(t) = mean ICP (mmHg) — measured via lumbar puncture, implanted sensor, or eShunt gradient
x2(t) = ICP pulse amplitude (mmHg) — measured via high-resolution ICP waveform (P1/P2 ratio, amplitude)
x3(t) = central venous pressure CVP (mmHg) — measured via right heart cath or jugular venous pressure
x4(t) = sigmoid sinus pressure (mmHg) — measured via venous manometry during VSS or via implanted sensor
x5(t) = anterior SSS pressure (mmHg) — measured via venous manometry (the 2026 study found this predicts outcomes)
observation_model.measurement_frequency: Episodic (during procedures) for x3-x5; continuous (if implanted) for x1-x2
observation_model.what_is_measurable_NOW: x1 (mean ICP) is routinely measurable. x2 (pulse amplitude) requires waveform analysis. x3-x5 require invasive venous manometry (episodic only).
observation_model.what_requires_NEW_sensing: Continuous x3-x5 (continuous venous sinus pressure monitoring) does not exist. This is a SENSING gap, not a state-estimation gap.

components.name: venous congestion burden
components.description: The degree to which venous outflow is insufficient relative to CSF production, causing venous backup that is NOT reflected in mean ICP. v(t) is high when CVP is elevated AND sinus pressure distribution is abnormal AND the venous system cannot compensate.
components.observable_manifestation: High v(t) → elevated x3 (CVP), abnormal x4/x5 ratio (distribution), elevated x2 (ICP pulse amplitude due to venous congestion transmitted to CSF). But mean ICP (x1) may remain normal because CSF drainage (eShunt) compensates for the mean pressure while venous congestion persists.
components.why_it_is_LATENT: v(t) is not directly measurable. It must be INFERRED from the combination of x3, x4, x5, and x2. No single measurement captures it. Mean ICP (x1) does not reflect it because the eShunt/VSS drains CSF independently of venous congestion.

components.name: cranial compliance state
components.description: The compliance of the intracranial system (dura, brain tissue, venous sinuses) — how much the intracranial volume can change per unit pressure change. c(t) is the INVERSE of elastance. The 2026 study proposed increased dural compliance as a mechanism for worse outcomes.
components.observable_manifestation: Low c(t) (stiff system) → high x2 (ICP pulse amplitude) for a given cardiac output. High c(t) (compliant system) → low x2 but abnormal pressure-volume relationship. The PULSE AMPLITUDE (x2) carries compliance information that MEAN ICP (x1) does not.
components.why_it_is_LATENT: c(t) is not directly measurable in clinical practice. It must be INFERRED from the relationship between x2 (pulse amplitude) and x1 (mean ICP), potentially using infusion-test principles or model-based estimation.

components.name: treatment failure risk
components.description: The probability that the patient will experience symptomatic recurrence (R2-C3 phenotype) within time horizon H, given the current venous congestion burden v(t) and compliance state c(t).
components.observable_manifestation: r(t) is a PREDICTION, not a measurement. It manifests as future headache recurrence despite normal x1 (mean ICP).
components.why_it_is_LATENT: r(t) is a future outcome that has not yet occurred. It must be PREDICTED from the current latent state z(t) = [v(t), c(t)] using a model trained on historical data.

what_makes_z_identifiable: v(t) is identifiable IF we have x3 (CVP), x4 (sigmoid pressure), x5 (anterior SSS pressure) simultaneously — because the COMBINATION of these signals constrains the venous congestion state in a way that no single signal does.

c(t) is identifiable IF we have x1 (mean ICP) AND x2 (ICP pulse amplitude) simultaneously — because the RATIO of pulse amplitude to mean ICP carries compliance information (this is the principle of infusion testing, but applied to spontaneous pulsations).
r(t) is identifiable IF we have longitudinal data (z(t) over time) + outcome labels (which patients actually failed) — because the prediction model must be trained on historical outcome data.
The CRITICAL identifiability question: can two different z(t) states produce the same X(t) observations? This is the IDENTIFIABILITY TEST (Step 4 below).

prediction_model.outcome_y_tH: y(t+H) = headache recurrence (binary: 0=no recurrence, 1=recurrence) at time horizon H (e.g., H=6 months)
prediction_model.time_horizon: H = 3-12 months (the 178-patient study found recurrence at mean ~390 days ≈ 13 months)
prediction_model.uncertainty_propagation: Bayesian: posterior P(z(t) | X(1:t)) → posterior predictive P(y(t+H) | X(1:t)). The uncertainty in z(t) propagates to uncertainty in y(t+H).
prediction_model.what_makes_this_predictive: The model must be trained on a dataset where X(t) and y(t+H) are both known — i.e., patients with multi-signal measurements AND documented headache recurrence outcomes. This dataset does NOT currently exist — it would need to be collected prospectively.

interventions: If v(t) is high AND c(t) is normal → venous congestion is the problem → consider venous intervention (repeat VSS, longer stent, CPAP for OSA)
If c(t) is abnormal AND v(t) is normal → compliance is the problem → consider CSF compliance modification (shunt adjustment, medical therapy)
If both v(t) and c(t) are abnormal → combined problem → multi-modal intervention
If r(t) is low → no intervention needed → continue monitoring
If r(t) is high AND v(t) and c(t) are normal → consider non-physiological cause (migraine, central sensitization) → refer to headache specialist
action_policy.what_makes_this_different_from_existing: Existing systems use ONE variable (ICP) and ONE intervention (drainage adjustment). This policy uses THREE latent variables (v, c, r) and selects between FIVE intervention types.

parameters_theta: Venous hemodynamic parameters (resistance, compliance of venous pathways)
CSF dynamics parameters (production rate, absorption capacity, cranial compliance)
Prediction model parameters (weights relating z(t) to y(t+H))
These parameters are patient-specific and must be estimated from individual data

what_exists_in_adjacent_domains.existing: Multi-variable hemodynamic state estimation in cardiac ICU (e.g., estimating cardiac output, vascular resistance, and compliance from arterial waveform + CVP + other signals). This is well-established in critical care.
what_exists_in_adjacent_domains.collision_with_proposed: MODERATE — the CONCEPT of multi-variable physiological state estimation exists in cardiac care. But it has NOT been applied to IIH or CSF-venous physiology.

what_exists_in_adjacent_domains.existing: ICP waveform analysis for compliance estimation (P1/P2 ratio, pulse amplitude analysis). Research literature exists on inferring compliance from ICP waveform.
what_exists_in_adjacent_domains.collision_with_proposed: MODERATE — the concept of estimating compliance from ICP waveform EXISTS. But it has NOT been combined with venous pressure signals for IIH treatment failure prediction.

what_exists_in_adjacent_domains.existing: Digital twin concepts for intracranial physiology (model-based estimation of CSF dynamics, cerebral blood flow, etc.). Research-stage, not clinical.
what_exists_in_adjacent_domains.collision_with_proposed: LOW-MODERATE — the concept of model-based physiological state estimation exists. But no digital twin combines venous + CSF + compliance signals for IIH.

what_exists_in_adjacent_domains.existing: Continuous ICP monitoring with trend analysis and prediction of future ICP changes. Clinical studies exist.
what_exists_in_adjacent_domains.collision_with_proposed: MODERATE — the concept of ICP prediction exists. But it predicts ICP (an OBSERVABLE), not a LATENT venous/compliance state. And it uses ICP alone, not multi-modal venous+CSF signals.

what_exists_in_adjacent_domains.existing: Closed-loop control of physiological variables (e.g., blood glucose, blood pressure, anesthesia depth). Well-established in other domains.
what_exists_in_adjacent_domains.collision_with_proposed: LOW — closed-loop control exists in other domains but NOT for IIH treatment using venous state.

broad_prior_art_attack.the_critical_question:
Does any prior system perform the SAME TRANSFORMATION:
  multi-modal longitudinal venous + CSF signals → latent state → future failure prediction → intervention selection?

ANSWER: NO system found that performs this SPECIFIC transformation.
BUT: the COMPONENTS (state estimation, prediction, waveform analysis) exist in adjacent domains. The NOVELTY is in the COMBINATION applied to the IIH failure-prediction problem, not in any single component.
broad_prior_art_attack.honest_assessment:
The broad idea of 'physiological state estimation from multiple signals' is NOT novel — it exists in cardiac care, ICU monitoring, and digital twin research. What MAY be novel is:
  (a) the SPECIFIC latent state (venous congestion burden + cranial compliance)
  (b) the SPECIFIC prediction target (R2-C3: headache recurrence despite normal ICP)
  (c) the SPECIFIC intervention selection (non-drainage interventions based on venous state)
  (d) the COMBINATION of multi-compartment venous + CSF signals for IIH

The novelty is in the APPLICATION and SPECIFIC STATE, not in the general method.

novelty_layers.what_it_is: The specific latent state z(t) = [v(t) venous congestion, c(t) cranial compliance, r(t) failure risk]
novelty_layers.is_it_novel: PARTIALLY — venous congestion and cranial compliance are known physiological concepts. The COMBINATION as a 3-component latent state for IIH treatment is novel. But each component individually is known.
novelty_layers.what_would_make_it_novel: If the SPECIFIC COMBINATION of v(t) + c(t) predicts R2-C3 recurrence BETTER than any single variable. This requires validation.

novelty_layers.what_it_is: The method of inferring z(t) from X(t) — i.e., the observation model h(z,θ) and estimation algorithm
novelty_layers.is_it_novel: PARTIALLY — Bayesian state estimation, Kalman filtering, and model-based inference exist in other domains. The APPLICATION to multi-compartment venous + CSF signals for IIH is novel.
novelty_layers.what_would_make_it_novel: If the SPECIFIC observation model (how x1-x5 map to v,c,r) is physiologically grounded and validated. The model structure matters, not just the estimation method.

novelty_layers.what_it_is: Predicting y(t+H) = headache recurrence from z(t)
novelty_layers.is_it_novel: NOVEL AS APPLIED — ICP prediction exists, but predicting HEADACHE RECURRENCE DESPITE NORMAL ICP from a VENOUS/COMPLIANCE state is novel. No existing system predicts this specific phenotype.
novelty_layers.what_would_make_it_novel: If the prediction is VALIDATED — i.e., if z(t) actually predicts R2-C3 recurrence in a prospective study.

novelty_layers.what_it_is: Selecting intervention based on z(t) — the decision rule π(z) → intervention
novelty_layers.is_it_novel: NOVEL — no existing system selects between intervention types (venous intervention, CSF modification, CPAP, migraine referral) based on a latent physiological state. Existing systems only adjust drainage.
novelty_layers.what_would_make_it_novel: If the policy is VALIDATED — i.e., if selecting intervention based on z(t) improves outcomes vs. current practice.

identifiability_test.test_question: Can two different z(t) states produce the same X(t) observations?

test_cases.case: Case 1: High v(t) (venous congestion) + Low c(t) (stiff compliance) vs. Low v(t) + High c(t) (compliant)
test_cases.observations_case_A: x1=12 (normal ICP), x2=4 (elevated pulse — from stiff compliance), x3=14 (elevated CVP — from venous congestion), x4=10, x5=15 (abnormal distribution)
test_cases.observations_case_B: x1=12 (normal ICP), x2=4 (elevated pulse — from high compliance, different mechanism), x3=6 (normal CVP), x4=8, x5=8 (normal distribution)
test_cases.are_these_distinguishable: YES — x3 (CVP) and x4/x5 (sinus distribution) distinguish them. Case A has elevated CVP and abnormal distribution (venous congestion). Case B has normal CVP and distribution (compliance problem only). The MULTI-COMPARTMENT signals resolve the ambiguity.
test_cases.implication: v(t) IS identifiable when x3, x4, x5 are available. The multi-compartment measurement is ESSENTIAL — without it, the two cases are indistinguishable (same x1, x2).

test_cases.case: Case 2: Venous congestion causing headache vs. Migraine causing headache (both with normal ICP)
test_cases.observations_case_A: x1=12, x2=4, x3=14, x4=10, x5=15 (abnormal venous state)
test_cases.observations_case_B: x1=12, x2=3, x3=6, x4=8, x5=8 (ALL normal — no venous abnormality)
test_cases.are_these_distinguishable: YES — if all venous signals are normal (Case B), the headache is NOT caused by venous congestion. It is likely a separate headache disorder (migraine). The venous state estimation DISTINGUISHES IIH-related headache from non-IIH headache.
test_cases.implication: The latent state v(t) can DISTINGUISH between IIH-related and non-IIH headache. This is the TECHNICAL EFFECT: the system can tell the physician 'this headache is venous' vs. 'this headache is not venous — refer to headache specialist.'

test_cases.case: Case 3: Rising v(t) trajectory (predicting future failure) vs. Stable v(t) (no failure predicted)
test_cases.are_these_distinguishable: YES — the TEMPORAL TRAJECTORY distinguishes them. The same instantaneous value (x3=8) can be part of a rising trajectory (Case A at earlier time) or a stable trajectory (Case B). The TRAJECTORY, not the instantaneous value, carries predictive information.
test_cases.implication: r(t) (failure risk) is identifiable from the TRAJECTORY of z(t), not just the instantaneous value. This requires LONGITUDINAL measurement — a single time point is insufficient.

test_cases.case: Case 4: Can v(t) and c(t) trade off? (high v + high c vs. low v + low c, same x1 and x2?)
test_cases.observations_case_A: x1=12, x2=4 (from high v → venous congestion raises pulse + low c → stiff raises pulse; effects ADD)
test_cases.observations_case_B: x1=12, x2=4 (from normal v + normal c, but patient has migraine causing symptoms; pulse is 4 for unrelated reasons)
test_cases.are_these_distinguishable: YES if x3-x5 are available — Case A would show abnormal venous signals, Case B would not. NO if only x1 and x2 are available — both produce the same mean ICP and pulse amplitude.
test_cases.implication: The latent state z(t) = [v, c] is identifiable ONLY with multi-compartment signals (x3-x5). Without venous signals, the state is NOT identifiable — which is exactly why current ICP-only systems cannot distinguish these cases.

identifiability_test.identifiability_verdict:
The latent state z(t) = [v(t), c(t)] IS identifiable from the multi-compartment signal set X(t) = [x1, x2, x3, x4, x5], but ONLY when:
  (a) multi-compartment venous signals (x3, x4, x5) are available
  (b) longitudinal trajectory data is available (not just instantaneous)

WITHOUT venous signals, the state is NOT identifiable — which explains why current ICP-only systems cannot predict R2-C3 recurrence.

This is the TECHNICAL EFFECT: the multi-compartment venous state estimation RESOLVES an ambiguity that single-variable ICP measurement cannot. This is not just 'more data' — it is a fundamentally different capability.
identifiability_test.the_technical_effect:
The specific technical effect that prior systems cannot obtain is:
  DISTINGUISHING between IIH-related headache (venous congestion cause)   and non-IIH headache (migraine/other cause) in patients with normal ICP.

No existing system can make this distinction because no existing system measures multi-compartment venous state. The technical effect is NOT 'better measurement' — it is RESOLVING A CLINICAL AMBIGUITY that currently leads to misdiagnosis (treating migraine as IIH recurrence) or missed diagnosis (treating venous congestion as migraine).

verdict.the_state_is_defined: z(t) = [v(t) venous congestion burden, c(t) cranial compliance state, r(t) failure risk]
verdict.the_state_is_identifiable: YES — with multi-compartment venous signals (x3-x5) + longitudinal trajectory. WITHOUT venous signals, it is NOT identifiable.
verdict.the_technical_effect: DISTINGUISHING IIH-related headache (venous) from non-IIH headache (migraine) in patients with normal ICP — resolving a clinical ambiguity that current systems cannot.
verdict.the_novelty_is_in: Layers 3+4 (prediction of R2-C3 + action policy selecting non-drainage interventions). Layers 1+2 (state representation + inference) exist in adjacent domains but have NOT been applied to this specific problem.
what_must_be_proven_before_mechanism: 1. PREDICTIVE VALIDITY: does z(t) actually predict R2-C3 recurrence? (prospective study)
2. PATENTABILITY: is the combination of multi-compartment venous state estimation + R2-C3 prediction + intervention selection patentable? (prior-art search at the CLAIM level)
3. CLINICAL UTILITY: does selecting intervention based on z(t) improve outcomes vs. current practice? (clinical trial)
4. IMPLEMENTABILITY: can the system be built with available sensing technology? (engineering assessment)
verdict.gate_status: YELLOW → APPROACHING GREEN — the state is mathematically defined, identifiable, and has a specific technical effect. But predictive validity and patentability are not yet proven.
verdict.mechanism_status: UNPROPOSED — the next step is to prove predictive validity (does z(t) predict R2-C3?) and patentability (is the combination novel at the claim level?). Only then can mechanism generation begin.
